correctness.rationale: The stationary tagged-age sum has finite positive exponential moments exactly for θ<r q_k/k, by symmetric-convex Poisson-void bounds and a matching diagonal survival lower bound. Matching conditional Gaussian Chernoff and Mills bounds give the excursion exponent; the falling-factorial formula for q_k/q_1 proves strict batch-size ordering. The conditional variance normalization is 2D A_i; all statements are for finite fixed N,m,k,D,r. The θ=r q_k/k boundary is divergent, not merely an upper moment bound. An independent pair-shock quadrature and finite factorial-identity checker provide reproducibility but do not prove infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: The exact joint excursion rate quantifies correlated spatial extremes of k tagged particles, a physically interpretable many-body diagnostic of batch-reset synchrony. Unlike the nonmonotone two-point covariance reported in the source, the marginal-normalized extreme rate strictly orders all integer batch sizes from m=1 to m=N for every k>=2, including intermediate partially simultaneous resets. The age-moment threshold is an exact structural mechanism and not an arbitrary fixed-parameter tabulation. The result does not claim a new first-passage theory or prefactors.
